How does hourly-to-salary conversion work?

Hourly wage to annual salary

Hourly rate × hours per week × paid weeks

Use your regular schedule and subtract any unpaid weeks.

$25 × 40 × 52 = $52,000

Annual salary to hourly wage

Annual salary ÷ annual scheduled hours

A 40-hour week over 52 weeks adds up to 2,080 hours.

$60,000 ÷ 2,080 = $28.85/hr

2,080 is a baseline, not a rule. Forty hours for 52 paid weeks equals 2,080 paid hours. Change the schedule to match your work. See how many work hours are in a year for how the baseline is derived.

Examples with different schedules

Part-time at $20/hour

$20 × 30 hours × 52 weeks = $31,200

The hourly rate stays fixed. Fewer hours reduce the annual total.

Unpaid leave at $30/hour

$30 × 40 hours × 50 weeks = $60,000

Two unpaid weeks reduce earnings from the $62,400 baseline.

Does this show take-home pay?

Wage conversions show earnings before deductions. A bank deposit may be lower after taxes, benefit premiums, retirement contributions, and other payroll deductions. The paycheck calculator can subtract amounts you enter. It does not calculate taxes.

What if you work overtime?

If extra hours are paid at another rate, calculate them separately. At a $25 regular rate, 1.5× means $37.50 per overtime hour. Use the overtime calculator to compare rates and extra hours.

Frequently asked questions

How does the hourly-to-salary calculator handle my schedule?

Enter your regular hours per week and paid weeks per year. The tool multiplies your hourly rate by those two numbers, so part-time and seasonal schedules use the same math with your own inputs.

Do the results update when I change my hours?

Yes. Every result on this page recalculates instantly as you type — try changing 40 hours to 30 and watch the annual figure adjust.

How do unpaid weeks affect the annual figure?

Unpaid weeks are subtracted from the year before multiplying. At $25 an hour and 40 hours a week, 52 paid weeks give $52,000 while 50 paid weeks give $50,000.

Does this calculator include overtime or taxes?

No. Overtime is modeled separately on the overtime calculator, and all figures here are gross pay before taxes and deductions.

Hourly-to-salary methodology

Visible assumptions. Checkable formulas.

Regular annual pay is hourly wage × regular weekly hours × paid weeks. Monthly pay is annual total ÷ 12. Extra overtime is calculated separately. Values retain full precision until display. Read our calculation methodology.
